title: AWS accountId validation still enforces exactly 12 numeric digits after any credential-form change
description: Quick regression re-check for the accountId /^\d{12}$/ rule (config.controller.js) whenever the onboarding form is touched, to catch an accidental loosening or tightening of the regex.
steps: Enter a 12-digit numeric accountId and submit
expectedResult: The 12-digit value is accepted; the 11-digit value is rejected with the accountId format error, unchanged from prior behavior.

title: Cancel action is unavailable for scans already in a terminal status
preconditions: A scan exists in status 'completed' and another in 'failed'
steps: Open each scan's detail page and look for a 'Cancel Scan' control
expectedResult: No cancel control is shown/enabled for scans in 'completed' or 'failed'; if invoked directly via API it is rejected as a conflict rather than silently succeeding.

title: Dashboard security score changes after a new scan completes with a different pass/fail mix
steps: Note the current overall security score
Run a new scan that introduces at least one new FAIL finding
Reload the dashboard once the scan completes
expectedResult: The overall security score changes to reflect the new pass/fail ratio; it is not a static/cached value that ignores the latest scan.

title: Toggling a recurring scan schedule off stops further automatic scans from firing
preconditions: A project has an active recurring schedule
steps: Disable the recurring schedule from the UI
Wait past what would have been the next scheduled run time
expectedResult: No new scan is created after the schedule is disabled; the schedule document's status no longer reads 'scheduled_recurring' so the scheduler's runDue() query does not pick it up.

title: Connection health badge on the configure page reflects the most recent test result after reload
preconditions: A provider's most recent connection test failed
expectedResult: The provider's connection status badge shows the failed state with the message and timestamp from connectionHealth, not a stale 'verified' badge from an earlier successful test.
